first_impression.reaction: I typed 'wedding in crete' on the train. The second sentence tells me when to go and the third tells me which end of the island does what. That's basically my answer in the first 80 words, no pop-up, no waffle. I'd read the takeaways, jump to the best-time section, glance at the six venues and the ten questions, then the FAQ. Then bookmark.

journey.quote: A wedding in Crete suits late spring and early autumn, when the island is warm and dry without the full weight of July and August.
journey.reaction: There it is, second sentence, my exact search words. Good.

journey.quote: Long-term averages put most of Crete's rain between October and April, and spring and autumn bring milder heat than high summer.
journey.reaction: Fine, but 'spring and autumn' is a bit vague for a takeaway. Which months? I have to go down to the table to find out it's May and September.

journey.quote: The east around Elounda and Agios Nikolaos suits resort weddings, while Rethymno and Chania in the west suit harbour towns and smaller venues.
journey.reaction: Useful. That's the one I'd remember. I didn't know the island split like that.

journey.quote: Crete is the largest island in Greece, with more than 1,000 kilometres of coastline.
journey.reaction: Nice, but I already picked Crete. I'd scroll past this to get to the months.

journey.quote: | Month | Heraklion average | Heraklion average high | Heraklion rain days | Chania area average high | Chania area rain days |
journey.reaction: Six columns on a phone means sideways scrolling. And 'Heraklion average' next to 'Heraklion average high' made me stop. Average what?

journey.quote: May and late September sit between those extremes.
journey.reaction: This is the sentence I actually needed. Wish it were in the takeaways.

journey.section: Venue season windows and ceremony times
journey.reaction: Oh, practical. I hadn't thought about ceremony time at all. I'd screenshot this list.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, [Smartraveller](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/europe/greece) advises that wildfires occur in Greece during the extended summer period from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations, and can start with little warning, prompting evacuations.
journey.reaction: Dated this month, so yes, still true in 2026. A bit scary, but I'd rather know before I pick July.

journey.section: Six venues from east to west
journey.quote: These six show the range, from resort coast to hilltop garden.
journey.reaction: Short list, one line each, east to west. Easy to skim on a phone. I'd tap through to the venues guide from here.

journey.section: Choosing an area and a venue
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: AUD? I'm in Singapore. Is this just for Australians?

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: Two Crete quotes with the same guest list can land far apart, and rarely because one venue is simply dearer.
journey.reaction: Good opener. No numbers in this section, so 'just tell me how much it costs' doesn't get answered, but the bold lead-ins let me skim what changes the bill.

journey.quote: Put the same questions to each venue, and ask for the answers in writing.
journey.reaction: Ten numbered questions. This is the bit I'd bookmark and send on.

journey.quote: From Agios Nikolaos, Minos Beach Art Hotel puts Chania Airport at a 180-minute drive.
journey.reaction: Three hours! Glad I know that before I pick a venue on the wrong side.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.
journey.reaction: Written for Australians. Not my country, so I skip to the next heading. Labelled clearly enough that I don't mind.

journey.quote: That depends on the heat and rain you are comfortable with.
journey.reaction: First FAQ is my exact question and it opens with 'it depends'. The intro gave a straighter answer than the FAQ does.

journey.quote: Choose the end of the island by where your guests will land.
journey.reaction: Simple rule I can actually use.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a wedding in Crete cost? Even a ballpark. There isn't one number on the page.
How many months ahead should we book the venue? The timeline covers paperwork weeks, not when to lock in the date.
Is the Wedded Advisor service for people outside Australia, or only Australians?

turn_offs_found.quote: | Month | Heraklion average | Heraklion average high | Heraklion rain days | Chania area average high | Chania area rain days |
turn_offs_found.why: On a phone a six-column table means scrolling sideways and losing the month column. 'Heraklion average' sitting beside 'Heraklion average high' doesn't say it's the average temperature, so I had to stop and guess. A shorter table, or a plainer column name, would be readable on the train.

turn_offs_found.quote: That depends on the heat and rain you are comfortable with.
turn_offs_found.why: The first FAQ is exactly what I searched, and it opens with a hedge. If I jump straight to the FAQ, which I often do, I want the months in the first words, then the 'it depends'.

turn_offs_found.quote: Long-term averages put most of Crete's rain between October and April, and spring and autumn bring milder heat than high summer.
turn_offs_found.why: Takeaways are the part I actually read, and this one never names a month. The answer (May and late September) is buried in the body under the table.

turn_offs_found.quote: Crete is the largest island in Greece, with more than 1,000 kilometres of coastline.
turn_offs_found.why: Minor. A whole 'why Crete' section sits between the takeaways and the months, so it's one more screen of scrolling before the answer. Not a deal-breaker since the intro already answered me.

would_share_with: My cousin who's just started looking at Greek islands; I'd send her the ceremony-times list and the ten questions to ask every venue

cta_reaction.quote: Once you know which end of the island suits your guests, [talk to Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-in-crete&utm_content=primary).
cta_reaction.why: I'm just looking, I haven't picked an end of the island yet. No pop-ups and the links didn't get in my way, so no complaints. I'd bookmark before I'd enquire, and the AUD line leaves me unsure whether they'd work with someone in Singapore.

top_3_changes: Name the months in the first takeaway, for example that May and late September give mild highs with few rain days, so the takeaways answer 'when' on their own.
Open the 'When is the best time to get married in Crete?' FAQ answer with the months first, then the 'it depends' detail.
Make the month-by-month table phone-friendly: rename 'Heraklion average' to say it is the average temperature, and consider trimming columns or splitting it so it reads without sideways scrolling.

Prices are deliberately not printed, including in the costs section; the missing ballpark is logged as an unanswered question only.
The title, fees, Wedded Privileges and company specifics (including the AUD and Australian focus) are deferred, so they are noted as reader reactions but kept out of top_3_changes.
